doc.title: Mark Soskin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 17, 2021

title: Playing with Herbie Mann and Stanley Turrentine; accompanying flute and tenor
summary: He played with Herbie Mann (Brazilian music), Turrentine and Rollins at once; Turrentine's My Romance and Sugar; playing softly behind flute.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Tell me about playing with Herbie Mann if you don’t mind.
He was a favorite of mine back then.

I played a lot with Herbie and yeah, at one time I was playing with Herbie, Stanley Turrentine and Sonny at the same time. And so it was great. I loved it. Mainly with Herbie it was playing Brazilian music and that’s pretty much what we did, Brazilian music. I mean Stanley completely different. It was like about — well I remember Stanley used to do “My Romance.” That was like his big tune that he used to do. And the sound that he had was so great — you know it was just heavenly.
You probably played “Sugar” a few times.
I played “Sugar,” yes. That was a must-do. So you know if you’re playing with somebody like that there’s certain things you really need to know.
Did you find that you played in different parts of the piano behind a flute player as opposed to a tenor sax player?
Definitely. Oh for sure. Now if you’re playing behind a flute player you’ve got to play pretty soft. So you know you’ve got to be aware of that, the dynamics. And I just did it.
